key_insight: Near-teacher in-distribution performance after on-policy distillation can mask lost out-of-distribution capabilities and incomplete multi-teacher consolidation.
engineering_relevance: Post-RL consolidation should test extrapolative and composed tasks explicitly rather than treating strong in-distribution scores as evidence of capability retention.
method: Evaluate OPD and multi-teacher OPD on synthetic reasoning and Qwen3-based math, coding, agent, and long-context tasks.
Probe teacher capability and training-data coverage as generalization bottlenecks; compare update geometry with RL baselines.
Propose geometry-based patching and base-preserving replay to improve OOD performance while largely preserving IND performance.
evidence_signal: In extrapolative evaluations, distilled models reached 96.04–102.73% of teacher IND scores but scored 2.45–16.25% below the base model on OOD tasks; across three compositional settings, MOPD scored 18.19–24.34% below the best teachers on composed tasks.
watch_item: Eliminating OOD forgetting required jointly addressing teacher capability and data coverage in the reported experiments; broader generalization remains unestablished.
paper_title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
